Starting as a regional American freight forwarder in 1991, their company became an international group combining cargo logistics with airline operations, supported by hubs and operating centres across several continents.

long_biography.plain_text:
Christopher J. Alf transformed National Air Cargo from freight forwarding into an integrated airline platform by acquiring Murray Air in 2006. Renamed National Airlines, the carrier added aircraft operations to the cargo network he had created. Regulatory approvals then broadened the group into scheduled and charter services for freight and passengers.

Alf made continuous performance review and round-the-clock shipment tracking part of the operating model. National developed hubs in the United States and centres across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, coordinating cargo fulfilment with aircraft scheduling. The group has used that structure for commercial transport, government logistics and humanitarian movements, including missions that require rapid deployment and specialist handling.
